svg.title: kV: volts rise with speed
svg.desc: Animated. A graph of volts against speed is a straight green line from zero: the volts it takes to hold a speed, kV times speed; a small triangle marks the slope as kV. A dot slides along the line to a low, a middle and a high speed and back. Beside it a wheel spins faster as the dot moves right, and a green volts bar on the same scale rises with it. A spinning motor is also a generator, pushing back against the battery (back-EMF); the push-back grows in a straight line with speed, so to hold a speed you must out-push it.
svg.text: kV × speed is what it takes to hold a speed.
A spinning motor is also a generator, pushing back (back-EMF), and the push-
back grows in a straight line with speed. To hold a speed you must out-push
it: kV is that slope, the volts added for each step of speed.
